title: The weight of Lot Seven
subtitle: Port of Melaka / Inbound customs docket 007

evidence.label: 01  Manifest
evidence.title: Signed declaration
evidence.text:
Chinese Porcelain Trader • Captain Lin • from Quanzhou
Owner: Lin trading house
Lot 7: six standard stacks of common bowls (60 bowls). No other goods declared.

evidence.label: 02  Exterior
evidence.title: Lot Seven on the quay scale
evidence.text: The lid is tied with a green cord. The scale reads 18 catties gross. The bonded jar and its packing are stamped 3 catties tare.

evidence.label: 03  Open jar
evidence.title: Beneath the lowest stack
evidence.text: All six stacks have intact stamped spacers. The reeds and paper are dry. Beneath them is an unlisted packet: three waxy, aromatic lumps with red crystalline grains on a broken edge.

evidence.label: 04  Captain
evidence.title: Captain Lin's account
evidence.text: “We weighed it at eighteen. I told the clerk it was damp packing. The cord came off an older shipment. Count the bowls if you like.”

rulings.label: Hold the lot for prohibited cargo

reasons.label: Use the green transit cord as proof of the contents.
Use the captain’s account of damp packing.
Compare the gross scale reading directly against the bowl weight.
Deduct the stamped tare and intact bowls; match the parcel to the manual.

hidden_truth.success: Amendment accepted. The intact bowls account for twelve catties; the dry jar and packing account for three. The remaining three are legal red-grain frankincense, liable for 18 extra duty when the ship trades.
hidden_truth.clear: Cleared as filed. No additional duty assessed.
hidden_truth.unsupported: The evidence cited did not support the amendment. The declaration stands; no additional duty assessed.
hidden_truth.hold: The hold stopped lawful trade: red-grain frankincense is declarable, not prohibited.
